java_locations.role: Creates POINT_FOR_ASSOCIATION under the endpoints' common Quark parent, or through quarkInContext when their parents differ. The latter puts the point in the association statement's current group.
Creates SVEK nodes by traversing top-level groups before root leaves and each group's direct leaves before child groups.
Paints Bibliotekon's insertion-ordered allNodes stream; an association point is not painted relative to its associated class.

rust_locations.role: Already records the cross-parent point owner as the current group, matching Java.
Already places AssociationPoint in the correct owner-local SVEK node stream.
Ignores AssociationPoint while consuming the node stream and instead paints every point immediately after entity C, which is wrong when C and the point have different owners.

claimed_invariant: Association-point paint order is the same owner-local SVEK node order used for layout and collision traversal. The point's associated class C does not determine its paint position. With cross-parent endpoints, a point owned by a later statement package paints after earlier top-level packages even when C belongs to an earlier endpoint package.
causal_divergence: The predecessor correctly records and lays out the point in the statement package, but render_plantuml_svg emits its ellipse in the entity-C loop. In checker2_cross_parent_statement_owner, C is in the first package while the point is in the third, so Rust paints the point before the east-package class; Java paints the east package first and reaches the point only in the third package's direct-leaf traversal. Root-owned and same-parent cases can accidentally pass because C and the point occur at compatible positions.
planned_model_change: Remove entity-C-relative association-point painting. When render_plantuml_svg consumes SvekNodeEmission::AssociationPoint, paint that point from the solved association layout slot (or the corresponding oracle point on the strict path). Keep ownership, geometry, layout graph construction, link order, and point styling unchanged.
perturbation_axes: statement package before versus after both endpoint packages
associated class C in the first endpoint package versus the second endpoint package
later direct leaf in the statement package versus no later leaf
acceptance: An independent checker creates fresh valid inputs crossing at least two listed axes and preserves every source, Java SVG, Rust SVG, command result, and diff under test-diagrams/perturbations/class-association-cross-parent-statement-owner-tree-position/.
Every fresh Java-success input is byte-exact through diff_one --no-oracle; any nonzero fresh diff rejects the change.
The preserved checker2_cross_parent_statement_owner counterexample becomes exact without changing point coordinates, layout constants, comparator policy, or baselines.
Fresh root-owned and same-parent controls remain exact, proving that paint order follows one node stream rather than a cross-parent special case.
Parser, renderer, perturbation, baseline-ratchet, and harness-guard tests pass at the reviewed implementation revision.
forbidden_approaches: branches keyed to fixture names, labels, package counts, source lines, or corpus membership
coordinate sorting, coordinate thresholds, point-position offsets, SVG post-processing, or golden reads
changing point ownership or layout topology when the recorded owner and layout stream are already correct
changing second-association lifecycle, link ordering, comparator slack, baselines, park lists, error markers, or allow-lists inside this mechanism
